deep.reconstruction:
The page has two unrelated notes from Hilbert's preparatory notebook, apparently from the period of the 1900 Paris problems.

(A) Lines 1–5 continue a to-do list from the previous page. That page asks for Abel's functional equations to be solved without assuming differentiability; this is the theme of Hilbert's 5th problem. Hilbert adds that Lie's claim should also be examined: that every real transformation (of a continuous group) can be regarded as generated by an infinitesimal one. In modern terms the claim is that every element g of a real Lie group lies in exp(Lie algebra). The reference is Lie on infinite groups, Abh. d. Kgl. sächs. Ges. d. Wiss. 1895, p. 48. No derivation is given.

(B) The main paragraph concerns the 'function-theoretic part of the problem': extending Kronecker's theorem that every abelian field over Q is a cyclotomic field (Kronecker–Weber) to arbitrary base fields. This is the programme of Hilbert's 12th problem.
- Heuristic models:
  - Archimedes repeatedly halved the full angle and so reached arbitrarily many points on the circle. Modern reading (mine): the 2^n-th roots of unity are reached by iterated square roots, cos(theta/2) = sqrt((1+cos theta)/2). This gives the tower Q ⊂ Q(i) ⊂ Q(zeta_8) ⊂ ... , in which each step has degree 2 and only the prime 2 ramifies.
  - Gauss, Werke Bd. 3, pp. 352 and 461. Very probably these are his Nachlass notes on the lemniscatic functions and the division of the lemniscate, which is the complex-multiplication analogue.
- Proposed method: over a given base field k, first determine all extensions K/k such that
  - the relative degree [K:k] is a power of 2, and
  - the relative discriminant d(K/k) is divisible only by primes dividing 2.
- In modern terms: study the 2-extensions of k unramified outside the primes above 2 (and infinity). These are the finite quotients of the Galois group G_S(2) with S = {primes above 2, infinite places}. Such fields are built as towers of relative quadratic extensions, each step ramified only above 2.
- The next page says these fields can be treated with the methods of 'my papers'. This plausibly means his theory of relative quadratic fields (1899).
- For k = Q the abelian part of this family is exactly the set of subfields of Q(zeta_{2^infinity}), consistent with Kronecker–Weber.
errors: None in the mathematics: there are no computations, only programmatic statements.

Lie's claim, taken literally for Lie groups, is false. In SL(2,R) the matrix diag(-2,-1/2) is not the exponential of any real traceless 2x2 matrix. Hilbert only marks it as something to check, so this is not an error of his.
The 2-power, unramified-outside-2 family captures only the 2-part of the ray class field tower. Hilbert presents it explicitly as a first step ('zunächst'), so this is not an error.

results.what: Question whether every element of a continuous transformation group is generated by an infinitesimal transformation (Lie's claim)
results.modern_name: Surjectivity of the exponential map for Lie groups; context of Hilbert's 5th problem
results.usually_credited_to: Lie (claim); counterexamples are classical (SL(2,R)); the 5th problem was solved by Gleason, Montgomery–Zippin and Yamabe in 1952–53

results.what: Programme to extend Kronecker's theorem (abelian fields over Q are cyclotomic) to arbitrary base fields
results.modern_name: Hilbert's 12th problem (Kronecker's Jugendtraum generalized); explicit class field theory

results.what: Concrete first step: determine all extensions of the base field of 2-power relative degree whose relative discriminant involves only primes dividing 2, modelled on angle bisection and Gauss's lemniscate division
results.modern_name: 2-extensions unramified outside 2; Galois groups with restricted ramification G_S(2); the Z_2-cyclotomic tower
results.usually_credited_to: Shafarevich (1960s), Koch, Iwasawa (1950s–60s) for the systematic theory

deep.surprise_reason: The 12th-problem programme and the 5th-problem theme are well known as Hilbert's. The specific suggestion to start with 2-power extensions ramified only above 2, by analogy with iterated angle bisection, is a nice unpublished detail. It foreshadows the study of restricted-ramification p-extensions and Z_p-towers. But it is only a heuristic sketch, with no results, so the surprise is modest.

checkable.asserts: Q(i) (first bisection step) has polynomial discriminant -4, a power of 2 up to sign.
The discriminant of Phi_16 is a power of 2 (it equals 2**32), so Q(zeta_16) is ramified only at 2. This is the tower of the 'Archimedes' model.
Half-angle formula: angle bisection needs only a square root, so each step is a quadratic extension.
2cos(pi/8) has minimal polynomial x**4-4*x**2+2, of degree 4 (a power of 2). It is Eisenstein at 2, hence ramified only at 2.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; a,b,c=symbols('a b c',real=True); M=Matrix([[a,b],[c,-a]]); simplify(M.eigenvals())
checkable.asserts: A real traceless 2x2 matrix has eigenvalues ±sqrt(a**2+b*c): either real ±lam, giving exp-eigenvalues e^{±lam} > 0, or ±i*mu, giving eigenvalues of modulus 1. Hence diag(-2,-1/2) is not exp of sl(2,R), contradicting Lie's claim as literally stated.

The '+' after 'Ausdehnung' is an insertion or reference mark in the margin, not '+ + +' text.
